title: Hermes, Serpent, Caduceus & Axis — Historical Lineages and Comparative Boundaries
purpose: Separate Hermes, Hermes Trismegistus, the caduceus, Asclepius' rod, kuṇḍalinī serpent, Egyptian uraeus/Wadjet and Potatoverse serpent/Axis comparisons before relating them to body anatomy.
epistemic_rule: Serpent/staff/axis motifs recur across traditions, but resemblance does not demonstrate common origin, anatomical encoding or a universal hidden doctrine. Historical meaning must be established within each tradition before cross-comparison.

attested_roles: god associated with boundaries and boundary markers
lineages.project_value: Hermes is a particularly strong comparator for Door/Boundary/Messenger/Passage because movement between domains belongs to his historical role.
lineages.boundary: Hermes is not historically a chakra deity or a neuroanatomical symbol.

lineages.historical_form: A herald's staff. Early descriptions/forms need not begin as a modern winged double-snake emblem; later canonical forms show two intertwined serpents, sometimes with wings.
historical_functions: commerce and negotiated peace in later reception
lineages.project_value: Central staff + paired serpents is visually useful for Axis + paired-channel comparison.
lineages.hard_boundary: Do not claim that the caduceus depicts spinal cord, sympathetic trunks, iḍā/piṅgalā, DNA or kundalini. Those are modern comparisons unless separately sourced.

lineages.form: one serpent coiled around one staff; no Hermes wings
lineages.meaning: healing/medicine through the cult and iconography of Asclepius
lineages.distinction: The Rod of Asclepius and Hermes' caduceus are historically different symbols. Modern medical use of the caduceus is comparatively recent and often treated as a confusion of the two.
lineages.project_value: Healing-serpent lineage should be separate from Messenger-serpent lineage.

lineages.formation: A Hellenistic/late-antique synthesis identifying Egyptian Thoth with Greek Hermes and attributing revelatory, philosophical, astrological, alchemical and other writings to the sage/divine teacher Hermes Trismegistus.
lineages.historical_setting: Roman Egypt and the wider late-antique Mediterranean; surviving Hermetic writings are Greek, Latin, Coptic and later transmitted in other languages.
lineages.boundary: Hermes Trismegistus is not simply the archaic Greek Hermes with a chakra system. The caduceus should not automatically be treated as the central diagram of philosophical Hermeticism.

lineages.historical_core: The term is related to 'coiled'; sources describe a feminine power/goddess in varied subtle-body systems. Systems differ: location, direction, number of cakras, channels and ritual functions are not universal.
lineages.important_variation: Modern scholarship notes systems in which kuṇḍalinī moves downward as well as upward, and systems where releasing a coiled obstruction permits breath to enter a central channel.
lineages.project_value: Coiling/uncoiling, activation, ascent/descent and central-channel imagery are legitimate comparative themes.
lineages.boundary: Kuṇḍalinī is not established neuroscience, electrical current, CSF or vagus anatomy.

lineages.placement: Frequently on royal/divine brow or crown; rearing cobras also protect sacred architecture.
lineages.project_value: Serpent-at-crown and guardian-at-threshold imagery can be compared to Crown/guardian themes.
lineages.boundary: Uraeus should not be equated with kundalini, caduceus or spinal anatomy.

lineages.note: Biblical serpent imagery is internally diverse (for example Edenic serpent, wilderness bronze serpent, later dragon/serpent receptions) and should not be reduced to one universal 'evil serpent' or merged with kuṇḍalinī/caduceus.
lineages.project_value: Maintain a separate biblical lineage and compare only after textual context is established.

structural_comparison.axis_staff: Vertical rod/staff/central-channel imagery is recurrent but tradition-specific.
structural_comparison.paired_serpents: Hermes' mature caduceus supplies a documented paired-serpent staff image.
structural_comparison.single_serpent: Asclepius supplies a documented single-serpent healing staff image.
structural_comparison.coiled_serpent: Kuṇḍalinī supplies a documented coiled-power/goddess motif in varied South Asian subtle-body systems.
structural_comparison.crown_serpent: Egyptian uraeus supplies a documented protective/royal serpent at the brow/crown.
structural_comparison.project_rule: These form a SERPENT FAMILY, not one historical symbol.

potatoverse_relations.boundary: do not force Father/Son or sympathetic-chain identity

nearest_comparators: Hermes as herald, traveler and psychopomp

potatoverse_relations.boundary: do not universalize every serpent as healing

modern_convergence_history.principle: Many apparent 'universal anatomy' diagrams are products of modern synthesis rather than evidence that ancient traditions all described the same body system.
modern_convergence_history.key_case: Vasant G. Rele (1927) explicitly physicalized yoga subtle anatomy by identifying suṣumṇā with spinal cord, iḍā/piṅgalā with sympathetic chains, sahasrāra with cerebrum, amṛta with CSF and kundalini with the vagus nerve. This is historically important as a modern reinterpretation, not accepted neuroanatomy.

anti_collapse_rules: Greek Hermes ≠ Hermes Trismegistus without qualification.
Hermes Trismegistus ≠ a historical founder of one unified ancient Hermetic church.
Uraeus ≠ third eye or kundalini by default.
Recurring serpent forms may be compared visually/functionally without claiming transmission.

sources.topic: Hermes as boundary god, psychopomp, messenger; caduceus
